prompt:
Repository: the Round Companion monorepo, checked out read-only at commit e02167f in the current directory (the app is under apps/web: src/ is the client, convex/ the backend, convex/ai/prompts/library the prompts; infra/ holds the AWS stack; docs/ at the root).
Extra read-only folders you may use: handoff-docs, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fqq-Desktop-Topflightapps-roundai/2a408671-6ff1-4104-9d24-9f97da7d0ee6/scratchpad/cr/review-evidence

Scenario TC-21/S19 — Doc review: surviving templates match prototype p72, SNF consult/discharge are built new, retention windows are config values on the server clock

Requirements it checks:
- T1: SNF Consult and SNF Discharge are built new, confirmed not present in the current prototype, not a port
- T2: Content and formatting of each surviving template still match the prototype exactly (TFA-94229)
- U7j: Retention windows are configuration values (not hard-coded), the clocks use server time, and the purge runs on the server

Given: Prototype RoundCompanion_PLAYGROUND_p72_HAIKU.html (TFA-94229), the app's templates, and convex/lib/lifecycle.ts plus the purge job
When: Compare section headings and formatting of the 6 surviving templates; confirm SNF consult/discharge are not ports; read where the retention windows and the clock come from
Then: The 6 survivors match exactly; 2 new SNF templates exist; every 3.6 window is a configuration value (not hard-coded), the clocks are server time, and the purge runs on the server
Oracle: Side-by-side review by a person. Facts to start from: on e02167f the windows are `as const` objects HOSPITAL_RETENTION / SNF_RETENTION in convex/lib/lifecycle.ts. Whether a source constant counts as the 'configuration value' 3.6 asks for (lengthened later under a hospital affiliation) is the reviewer's call. SNF consult/discharge are not built (known: TFA-92599 AC 2).

THE ORACLE WINS. The question below only scopes this scenario to what code can decide. If the question, or its pass/fail rule, ever reads differently from the Then/Oracle above, follow the Then/Oracle, give the verdict the oracle gives, and say where they differ in openQuestions.

Open questions the oracle defers to, with the oracle's default for each (do not settle them yourself):
- pending:signoff — oracle: "is the reviewer's call". Default: whether a source constant counts as the configuration value 3.6 asks for is the person's call: label that finding pending:signoff

Gaps the matrix already records (use the id in a label only when the finding is exactly that gap):
- known:no-snf-consult-discharge-templates — SNF consult and SNF discharge templates are not built (TFA-92599 AC 2) (matrix: "SNF consult/discharge are not built (known: TFA-92599 AC 2)")

YOUR QUESTION (answer this, from the code):
(a) Which note templates exist per context in the app (template registry / convex/ai/prompts/library/v1/templates and the code that offers them), and do SNF Consult and SNF Discharge templates exist? (b) Are the retention windows configuration values (not hard-coded), do the lifecycle/purge clocks use server time, and does the purge run on the server (a cron in convex/crons.ts or a server schedule) rather than being triggered by the client? You may compare the six surviving templates' section headings with the prototype (handoff-docs/RoundCompanion_PLAYGROUND_p72_HAIKU.html) and report differences as context.

pass = SNF consult and discharge templates exist, the windows are configuration values, the clocks are server time, and the purge runs on the server
fail = any of these is not so

Other halves of this scenario that another lane or a person runs (do not judge them; if the code you read predicts one of them, report that as a finding labelled half:<name>, supports = pass or fail):
- half:6 surviving templates vs p72 — a person's side-by-side (sign-off): "The 6 survivors match exactly"

Not part of this verdict (other scenarios, or notes that decide nothing here):
- purge cron registered on dev (CONFIG, Tim)



Label every finding:
- new: a failing point the matrix does not already record (supports = fail)
- known:<id>: exactly one of the recorded gaps listed above
- pending:<id>: a failing point whose verdict the oracle hands to one of the open questions above
- half:<name>: a point about one of the other halves above
- context: background, not for or against the verdict

Answer with: verdict (pass | fail | pending | unsure), answer (a short paragraph a QA lead can read: what the code does and why that is the verdict; name the recorded gaps and open questions it touches), findings (each with claim, file, line, quote, supports = pass | fail | context, label), physicianImpact, openQuestions, notDecidableByCode.
note: stdout is redacted (lib.mjs redactAll) before it is written; a run whose stdout held secret-like text not in the prompt is not written (stdout null, kinds in withheld)
